claim: Nice was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 2021 under the official name 'Nice, Winter Resort Town of the Riviera' as listing #1635.
quote: Nice, Winter Resort Town of the Riviera

claim: The UNESCO-inscribed perimeter centers on Nice's seafront and includes Belle Époque hotels such as Le Negresco and Westminster plus the Promenade du Paillon, with 152 UNESCO-emblem nails marking the boundary.
quote: 152 nails emblazoned with the UNESCO World Heritage emblem have been installed within the perimeter

claim: Nice was officially listed on 27 July 2021, with the UNESCO designation covering 522 hectares including the Promenade des Anglais, Old Town, south-east Nice and Port Lympia.
quote: on Tuesday, July 27, 2021, the city of Nice was officially listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site

claim: The Promenade des Anglais runs about 7 km from the airport to Quai des États-Unis and was begun in 1820, funded by Reverend Lewis Way and Nice's Anglican community.
quote: In 1820, when a particularly harsh winter further north brought an influx of beggars to Nice, some of the English proposed that the beggars could work on the construction of a walkway (chemin de promenade) along the sea.

claim: Cours Saleya hosts the flower market Tue–Sat 6:00–17:00 and Sun 6:00–13:30, the Marché Provençal food market Tue–Sun 6:00–13:30, a Monday antique market 7:00–18:00, and a summer evening artisan market (mid-May to mid-Sept) from 18:00 to 00:30.
quote: Tuesday to Saturday: 6.00 am to 5.00 pm | Sunday: 6.00 am to 1.30 pm ... Antique Market (Marché à la brocante) Monday: 7.00 am to 6.00 pm

claim: The free Ascenseur du Château elevator up to Castle Hill is located across from Castel Beach under the staircase, usually running 10:00–17:25 but with unreliable hours and occasional unannounced closures.
quote: The lift is usually open from 10 am to 5.25 pm but I have found this timeframe to be a bit unreliable

claim: Rick Steves recommends climbing Castle Hill at sunset with a picnic for 360-degree views over the Promenade and Alps, and characterizes Cours Saleya as a sensory medieval market for socca.
quote: sensational 360-degree views of the grand promenade and the spectacular Alps-to-Mediterranean scenery

claim: A self-guided Vieux Nice walk takes 2–3 hours and hits Cours Saleya, Cathédrale Sainte-Réparate at Place Rossetti, Palais Lascaris and the Chapelle de la Miséricorde.
quote: Visiting the Old Town of Nice can take 2 – 3 hours or longer

claim: Nice's beaches are pebble and split between free public sections (e.g. Beau Rivage public, Castel, Le Voilier, Coco) and private clubs charging roughly €20–€55 per lounger, with Beau Rivage sitting right at the Old Town edge.
quote: a privileged location on the border of the Old Town

claim: Nice has roughly 22 free public beaches spread across 7 km of coastline, most equipped with toilets and showers, so weekenders never need to pay a club to swim.
quote: 22 free public beaches stretched across 7 km of coastline

claim: Place Masséna is Nice's central square with a checkerboard pavement, the 1956 Fontaine du Soleil by Alfred Janniot featuring a statue of Apollo, and seven illuminated statues representing the continents that change color at night.
quote: Seven luminous statues, mounted on high masts, represent the seven continents and light up at night

claim: Lonely Planet's weekend plan suggests flying in Thursday evening for cheap fares and using Friday morning through Sunday evening for sightseeing, with walking as the best mode of transport across central Nice.
quote: Walking is the best way to get around town

claim: Buses #82 and #602 both leave Nice's Vauban station for Èze Village taking ~30 minutes, alternating roughly hourly, with #602 continuing to Monaco; avoid #600 which goes to Èze-sur-Mer instead.
quote: Two buses serve Eze Village: Bus #82 Plateau de la Justice and Bus #602 Monaco Casino. These alternate departures, so you'll have service approximately once hourly. Important: avoid Bus #600 Monaco, which goes to the seaside Eze-sur-Mer instead of the hilltop village.

claim: Combining Èze in the morning with Monaco in the afternoon is the classic pairing because cruise passengers flood Monaco in the morning and clear out by afternoon.
quote: Visiting Eze in the morning allows you to avoid a crush of tourists; visiting Monaco in the afternoon means missing cruise ship passengers which discharge in the morning.

claim: Lignes d'Azur bus #15 from Nice runs through Villefranche-sur-Mer to the Passable/Rothschild stop right at Villa Ephrussi de Rothschild's entrance, making it the easiest single-vehicle route to Cap Ferrat.
quote: Line 15 connects 'Port de Saint Jean Cap Ferrat - Promenade des Arts'... The bus line goes through Villefranche-Sur-Mer - a picturesque fishing village... Arrival: Passable / Rothschild

claim: Villa Ephrussi plus a Cap Ferrat coastal walk fills a comfortable full day of roughly 7 hours including transit, with 2–3 hours for the villa and 2 more for the cape.
quote: You should be able to visit Villa Ephrussi and walk along the Cape quite easily in a day, with about two to three hours for the Villa and another two hours for a walk, comfortably doing it in around 7 hours including the bus ride.

claim: TER trains from Nice to Cannes via Antibes run ~16 times daily with direct fares from €6, taking about 20 minutes to Antibes and 30–45 to Cannes.
quote: Fares start at just $6 USD per way, the average direct train journey is 20 minutes, and there are approximately 16 trains leaving per day

claim: Antibes' Musée Picasso is housed in Château Grimaldi where Picasso worked in 1946, and the recommended sequence is Cannes/Lérins in the morning then Antibes' Picasso Museum after the tour-bus crowds leave.
quote: Pablo Picasso set up a studio at the city's Château Grimaldi, which now houses the Picasso Museum... The best sequence is Cannes and the island(s) in the morning/early afternoon. Then train back to Antibes... You will hit the Picasso Museum at the best time of day—after the bus tours have gone.

claim: Ferries to the Lérins Islands depart from Cannes' Quai Laubeuf for a 15-minute crossing; Sainte-Marguerite round-trip starts at €16 and Saint-Honorat is €20.50 online.
quote: Round trip ferry tickets from Cannes to Ste Marguerite Island start from €16... Ferry tickets to Île Saint Honorat are 20.5 euros online and 22 euros in person for a round trip... The trip takes about 15 minutes from Cannes

claim: The old #400 bus is gone; the current route is TER to Cagnes-sur-Mer (15 min, €3.80) then Zou bus #655 to the Saint-Paul Village stop (30 min, €2.10), totalling about an hour for €5.90 each way.
quote: Regional Express Train (TER) from Nice-Ville to Cagnes-sur-Mer (15 min, €3.80), then Zou bus 655 to Village stop in Saint-Paul de Vence (30 min, €2.10)... €5.90 per person one-way

claim: Fondation Maeght's bus stop is before the village so riders should alert the driver; a summer 'Maeght-Matisse' shuttle (1 July–30 Sept, Tue–Sat, 5x/day) links the foundation, Saint-Paul, and Matisse's Rosary Chapel in Vence.
quote: The bus stop for the Fondation Maeght is before Saint Paul. Make sure you tell the driver you intend to stop there... from 1st July to 30 Sept. there is a 'Maeght-Matisse' navette (shuttle bus), which runs from Tuesday to Saturday, 5 times a day.

claim: TER trains from Nice-Ville to Menton take about 40 minutes with returns around €11–13, and right-side seats face the sea.
quote: The train from Nice Ville to Menton takes just 40 minutes... Tickets were £13.75 return... Sit on the right-hand side of the train when leaving Nice for beautiful sea views

claim: Menton works as either a 3–4 hour half-day (Old Town plus Cocteau Museum) or a 6–8 hour full day adding Val Rahmeh botanical garden and Plage des Sablettes.
quote: half-day = Old Town + museum (~3–4 hours)... A complete day allows 6–8 hours to add beach time, gardens, or nearby villages like Roquebrune-Cap-Martin.

claim: Villefranche-sur-Mer (5–15 min by TER) is a half-day port village highlighted for its citadel, hidden 'Rue Obscure' street, and sandy beach.
quote: Villefranche-sur-Mer... Picturesque village, fortress, 'Rue Obscure' hidden street, sandy beach... Travel Time: 5-15 minutes... Duration: Half day

claim: Musée Matisse in Nice charges €10 standard admission, opens 10am-6pm April-October (5pm winter), closed Tuesdays; €15 buys a 4-day pass to all Nice municipal museums.
quote: Standard ticket: €10... 4-day Nice Museums Pass: €15... daily except Tuesdays: November 1 – March 31: 10 am to 5 pm; April 1 – October 31: 10 am to 6 pm.

claim: The Matisse museum holds nearly 600 works including 57 sculptures (the largest public collection of his sculpture worldwide) and 38 paper cut-outs, housed in the 17th-century Villa des Arènes on Cimiez hill.
quote: nearly 600 works... 57 sculptures by Henri Matisse, representing the largest public collection of his sculptural works worldwide... 38 papiers gouachés découpés

claim: Musée National Marc Chagall in Nice opens daily except Tuesdays, charging €12 during exhibitions (€10 otherwise) and offering free admission the first Sunday of each month.
quote: Prices during exhibitions: Full rate: €12... Free admission is offered on the 1st Sunday of the month for all... open every day except Tuesdays

claim: MAMAC (Musée d'Art Moderne et d'Art Contemporain) closed on January 7, 2024 for a four-year renovation tied to the Promenade du Paillon 2 project, with works currently shown via its #MAMACnextdoor outside-the-walls programme.
quote: The MAMAC closed its doors on January 7, 2024 for renovation works and inclusion in the major Promenade du Paillon 2 project... #MAMACnextdoor to rediscover the museum's works

claim: Fondation Maeght in Saint-Paul-de-Vence costs €18 (€14 reduced, under 16 free) and opens daily 10am-6pm (until 7pm in July-August).
quote: Full price admission is €18, reduced tickets are €14, and children under 16 enter free... open daily from 10am to 6pm (10am to 7pm in July and August)

claim: Fondation Maeght is France's most important private art foundation, with works by Bonnard, Chagall, Miró, Giacometti, Calder and Braque integrated into Josep Lluís Sert's purpose-built architecture and gardens.
quote: France's most important private art foundation and hosts paintings and sculptures by artists including Bonnard, Chagall, Adami, Miró, Giacometti, Calder and Braque

claim: Villa Ephrussi de Rothschild on Cap Ferrat charges €18 full / €12 reduced for the standalone visit (€24 combined with Villa Kérylos, valid 8 days), with audio guide in nine languages included.
quote: Full rate: €18... Reduced rate: €12... Combined Ticket with Villa Kérylos — Full rate (26+): €24... Audio guides in nine languages are included.

claim: The pink Belle-Époque Villa Ephrussi sits between Villefranche and Beaulieu on Cap Ferrat, surrounded by nine themed gardens (French, Spanish, Florentine, stone, Japanese, exotic, Provençal, rose) overlooking the Mediterranean.
quote: surrounded by nine themed gardens: French garden, Spanish garden, Florentine garden, stone garden, Japanese garden, exotic garden, Provençal garden and rose garden

claim: The Cathédrale Saint-Nicolas in Nice — the largest Eastern Orthodox cathedral in Western Europe — is a working parish: visitors are welcome outside services, head coverings may be requested for women and bare shoulders/shirtless men are forbidden.
quote: Visiting is prohibited during services and ceremonies such as weddings... Women may be asked to cover their heads while inside... forbidden for men to visit the cathedral shirtless

claim: Musée Picasso in Antibes (housed in the 14th-century Château Grimaldi where Picasso worked in 1946) charges €12 adult admission, opens Tue-Sun 10am-6pm in summer, and is free for under-18s.
quote: Adult admission is €12... Tuesday through Sunday... 10:00–13:00 and 14:00–18:00 (September 16 – June 14), and 10:00–18:00 (June 15 – September 15)

claim: Hotel Negresco opened on the Promenade des Anglais in January 1913, designed by Belle-Époque architect Édouard Niermans with the pink-domed cupola attributed to Gustave Eiffel; it holds over 6,000 artworks across centuries.
quote: Architect Édouard-Jean Niermans utilized various architectural styles, including neoclassical, baroque, and rococo elements... the cupola and rounded frontage were not designed by Niermann but by Gustav Eiffel... more than 6,000 works of art

claim: The Palais de la Méditerranée, an Art Deco casino built 1928 by Charles and Marcel Dalmas for Frank-Jay Gould, was demolished in 1990 except for two facades which were classified as historical monuments and rebuilt as a hotel in the early 2000s for €120 million.
quote: constructed in 1928 by architects Charles Dalmas and his son Marcel for American millionaire Frank-Jay Gould... casino was completely demolished in May 1990, except for two of its facades... Rebuilt in the early 2000s for 120 million euros

claim: From Nice, the cheapest route to Fondation Maeght is tram 2 to Parc Phoenix then bus 9 to Vence (about an hour) connecting to bus 655 (€2.10, every 30 min weekdays); the Maeght stop is before Saint-Paul village so flag the driver.
quote: tram line number 2 to the Parc Phoenix stop, then take the 9 bus to Vence which takes about an hour. Then take bus 655 for the 5-minute ride... €2.10... departures of the 655 bus are every 30 minutes

claim: Chez Pipo, 13 rue Bavastro in the port district, has built its fame on socca, a wood-fired chickpea galette and undisputed star of its menu.
quote: Star incontestée de tous nos plats ! On lui doit la célébrité de Chez Pipo.

claim: René Socca, just off Rue Pairolière, is the no-frills budget pick for socca that locals favour.
quote: René Socca offers a straightforward and delicious experience, located just off Rue Pairolière, serving consistently good, fresh socca at very reasonable prices.

claim: Niçoise specialties to seek include socca, pissaladière (caramelised onions and anchovies on thin crust, no cheese), pan-bagnat, salade niçoise, petits farcis, daube, tourte de blettes and ratatouille.
quote: A cross between pizza and tart, made with caramelized onions, anchovies, and Niçois olives on a thin crust.

claim: An authentic salade niçoise contains only raw vegetables plus hard-boiled egg — no potatoes, no green beans — per Jacques Médecin's 1972 codification.
quote: A true Niçoise Salad only has raw vegetables, with the only cooked item being hard-boiled eggs. There are no green beans nor potatoes in this authentic recipe.

claim: Flaveur, run by the Tourteaux brothers, is the only two-Michelin-star restaurant in Nice, while Le Chantecler at Le Negresco holds one star alongside JAN, Les Agitateurs, ONICE, L'Aromate, Racines and Pure & V.
quote: As the only restaurant in Nice with two Michelin stars to its name, I know you can expect a stand-out experience

claim: Le Chantecler inside Hôtel Negresco on the Promenade des Anglais is led by MOF 2015 chef Virginie Basselot and pairs historic Belle Époque elegance with a summer terrace.
quote: MOF 2015, Virginie Basselot, is at the helm of its fine dining restaurant, Le Chantecler.

claim: Bistrot d'Antoine at 27 rue de la Préfecture holds a Michelin Bib Gourmand and is the go-to affordable French bistro in Vieux Nice (closed Sun-Mon; reservations essential).
quote: The restaurant has earned the Bib Gourmand designation for good quality, good value cooking.

claim: La Merenda, run by former two-Michelin-star chef Dominique Le Stanc, serves Niçoise classics (pissaladière, tripe niçoise, stockfish, tourte de blettes) with no phone, no credit cards, and in-person reservations only.
quote: It serves just twenty people, has a former head chef of a two Michelin starred restaurant and yet takes no reservations other than in person and does not even have a telephone.

claim: Chez Acchiardo is a 90-year-old family-run trattoria in Vieux Nice serving petits farcis niçois, salade niçoise and traditional grilled meats in a stone-walled dining room.
quote: Chez Acchiardo is a family-run restaurant located in the old town of Nice, serving traditional Italian cuisine for over 90 years.

claim: Olive & Artichaut on rue Sainte Réparate is a Bib Gourmand Mediterranean bistro that consistently scores top marks for value and creativity.
quote: Olive & Artichaut is a Bib Gourmand restaurant in the 2025 MICHELIN Guide France, recognized for good quality and good value cooking.

claim: Tourte de blettes, a chard tart studded with raisins and pine nuts that can be sweet or savoury, exemplifies the originality of Niçoise cuisine where vegetables are used in desserts.
quote: Chard pie is a perfect illustration of the originality of Niçoise cuisine, where vegetables are also used in sweet recipes.

claim: L'Effervescence in the Old Town is Nice's only champagne bar, pouring more than 80 champagnes alongside gourmet plates Tuesday–Saturday 6 pm–midnight.
quote: L'Effervescence is Nice's only champagne bar... serving gourmet food, sushi, fine wines and over 80 different kinds of champagne.

claim: Nice's private beach clubs along Promenade des Anglais charge roughly €35 single-lounger / €85 double with umbrella at Beau Rivage, with Opera Plage at €30 incl. umbrella and Ruhl Plage at €90 for a double set.
quote: Plage Beau Rivage Nice — Single lounger €35 per day; Double sunbed with umbrella €85. Opera Beach — Daily lounge chair rentals are priced at €30 and include an umbrella. Ruhl Plage — Double sun lounger with an umbrella and towel €90.

claim: Budgeting for a Nice private beach day for two people typically runs at least €100 once sunbeds, lunch and drinks are tallied.
quote: for a private beach for 2, count on dropping a hunsky at a minimum: a sunbed is 20€-50€ per person… anything you order for lunch will be 20€, 7€ on average for a glass of rosé or a coke.

claim: The Cap Ferrat sentier littoral is a roughly 6–7 km coastal loop around the Saint-Jean-Cap-Ferrat peninsula taking a half-day, with some rocky exposed sections despite its easy reputation.
quote: the full loop is roughly 6–7 kilometers (about 3.5–4.5 miles), and most people walk it as a half-day activity… some sections of the trail are steeper and more exposed than you might expect, with long stretches of rocky terrain, very little shade.

claim: Paloma Beach sits at the end of the most picturesque eastern stretch of the Cap Ferrat coastal path, while Plage de Passable bookends the western side with a beach club, café and public space.
quote: the final section of the sentier du littoral leading up to Paloma Beach is truly the most adorable and charming section… Plage Passable, a smallish beach with a beach club, cafe, and some public beach space.

claim: Plage de la Mala in Cap d'Ail is a secluded cliff-backed cove reached only via a long staircase, which keeps crowds thin even in peak summer and where waters consistently rank as the region's cleanest.
quote: Plage Mala is one of the most stunning beaches on the Côte d'Azur, a secluded spot surrounded by cliffs in the small town of Cap d'Ail… consistently rank as the cleanest sea water in the region. Because access is only down a long flight of stairs, the beach is usually free of crowds.

claim: Plage de la Garoupe on Cap d'Antibes offers fine sand with crystal-clear water at the entrance of the cape's coastal path and is recognised as a top swimming spot.
quote: The sandy beach of La Garoupe, at the entrance to the authentic coastal path, is famous for its crystal-clear waters… stunning natural setting with fine sand mixed with a few pebbles and crystal-clear water.

claim: Plage des Marinières at Villefranche-sur-Mer stretches roughly 1 km with shallow, calm water that makes it a locals' favourite swimming beach near Nice.
quote: Plage des Marinières beach stretches around 1 km along the bay… Nice locals choose Plage des Marinieres as their go-to place for swimming in the calm waters, and the shallow drop-off is reassuring to families.

claim: Mercantour National Park trailheads sit roughly 90 minutes to two hours from Nice by car, with a direct scenic train option to La Brigue making day hikes feasible.
quote: Mercantour National Park is easily accessible by direct scenic train from Nice to La Brigue, or most hikers choose to drive a rental car to the mountain trailheads, with the journey usually taking between ninety minutes and two hours.

claim: Vallée des Merveilles holds over 40,000 Bronze-Age rock carvings and can only be visited inside the protected zone with an accredited guide on roughly 2-hour tours.
quote: The red-rock valley is home to more than 40,000 rock carvings of animals and weapons dating from the Bronze age… Europe's largest open-air museum, highly protected and only accessible with an accredited guide, with tours lasting about 2 hours.

claim: The Esterel massif is a coastal volcanic range whose rhyolite rocks give the cliffs their distinctive red colour, peaking at Mont Vinaigre (618 m).
quote: soil and rocks of volcanic origin composed mainly of rhyolite, which gives the hills a red color. The highest point of the massif is Mont Vinaigre (618 metres or 2,028 feet).

claim: The Corniche d'Or (Route de la Corniche d'Or, the N98) is a roughly 30 km coastal drive between Saint-Raphaël and Cannes hugging the red Esterel cliffs.
quote: The Corniche d'Or (literally "golden cornice") is a 18.6 mile (30 km) drive along the coast of the Mediterranean Sea, from Saint Raphael to Cannes.

claim: Boat tours from Saint-Raphaël or Agay are the best way to see the Esterel's hidden calanques and sea caves inaccessible by land.
quote: For the most dramatic calanques, join a boat tour from Saint-Raphaël or Agay to get a whole new perspective on this dramatic section of coastline and access caves and secret coves that are impossible to reach by land.

claim: Horizon ferries run year-round from Cannes to Île Sainte-Marguerite roughly every 30 minutes between 9:00 and 17:30, with tickets from about €16 and a 15-minute crossing.
June on the Côte d'Azur typically delivers sea temperatures around 20 °C, daytime highs near 25 °C, and 10–12 hours of sunshine with only 20–30 mm of rain across ~4 days.
quote: the average sea temperature in June on the Côte d'Azur is around 20°C (68°F)… Maximum temperatures reach around 25°C (77°F)… You can expect around 10 to 12 hours of sunshine a day. Rainfall is generally low, with rainfall in Nice between 20 and 30 mm over 4 days on average.

claim: The Cap d'Ail sentier littoral runs roughly 3.6 km from Marquet Beach to Mala Beach and connects on to Monaco in about 1.5 hours total walking time.
quote: easy 3.6 km walk from Marquet beach, which opens onto the Principality of Monaco, to Mala beach… The walk to Monte Carlo (with the casino and Café de Paris) takes approximately 1.5 hours.

claim: The Mont Boron–Mont Alban loop above Nice is a moderately challenging hike averaging around 2 h 50 min with sweeping views over Nice, Villefranche bay and toward Cap Ferrat.
quote: a moderately challenging Mont Boron - Mont Alban route takes an average of 2 h 50 min to complete… sweeping panoramic views from the Cap Ferrat peninsula in the east all the way to the Esterel mountains in the west.

claim: Calanques National Park sits just outside Marseille and is best visited May–June, but its location west of Marseille places it many hours from Nice, making it impractical as a Nice-based weekend side trip.
quote: The best time to visit Calanques National Park is between May and June, with late spring/early summer weather being incredible… from June – September, reservations are required for some of the more popular areas.

claim: TER one-way fares from Nice-Ville: Villefranche €2.10 (5 min), Monaco €4.40 (20 min), Antibes €5.20 (25 min), Cannes €7.90 (40 min); trains run roughly every 15 minutes until ~10pm
quote: Villefranche-sur-mer: €2.10 (5 min); Monaco: €4.40 (20 min); Antibes: €5.20 (25 min); Cannes: €7.90 (40 min)... Trains run roughly every 15 minutes in both directions until around 10pm

claim: TER trains link Cannes to Ventimiglia along the coast, calling at all main Côte d'Azur towns; Nice-Ville is the main station
quote: TER (Trains Express Régionaux) provide a fast link between Cannes and Ventimiglia for all the main towns along on the Côte d'Azur coast

claim: Lignes d'Azur 2026 fares: single €1.70 (74 min transfers), 10-trip card €15, 24-hour pass €7, 7-day pass €20, monthly €45
quote: Single ride: €1.70; 10-trip card: €15.00; 24-hour pass: €7.00; 7-day pass: €20.00; Monthly subscription: €45.00

claim: Tram T2 connects Nice Côte d'Azur Airport to central Nice in 20-30 minutes for €1.70, running every 7-8 minutes weekdays from ~5:30am to ~11:55pm
quote: Tram Line 2 connects NCE directly to central Nice in 20-30 minutes... A tram to the airport runs every 7 to 8 minutes on weekdays... from 5.30 AM to 11.55 PM

claim: Nice has three tram lines: T1 (Henri Sappia–Hôpital Pasteur via Masséna/Garibaldi), T2 (airport to Port Lympia), T3 (airport to Saint-Isidore)
quote: Line T1 runs from Henri Sappia to Hôpital Pasteur... Line T2 connects the airport (Terminals 1 and 2) to the city center and Port Lympia... Line T3 primarily serves the western part of the city

claim: Bus #600 (which absorbed the old #100, #607 and #608 in April 2024) runs Nice-Villefranche-Beaulieu-Èze-sur-Mer-Cap-d'Ail-Monaco-Roquebrune-Menton every 15 min weekdays, 20 min Sundays; trip ~1 hour
quote: Since April 6, 2024, route 607... and route 608... merged to create route 600, the former route 100... The trip takes one hour, and the bus #600 leaves every 15 minutes during the week, and every 20 minutes on Sundays

claim: Bus #15 from Lycée Masséna runs to Villefranche-sur-Mer and Saint-Jean-Cap-Ferrat in ~15 minutes; takes the train back since #600 is often full returning from Monaco; service ends ~8-8:30pm
quote: Bus #15 Port de Saint-Jean - Departs from Lycee Massena bus stop... The journey takes approximately 15 minutes. Both buses run until around 8pm-8:30pm... Bus #600 is usually already full on its way back from Monaco

claim: Bus 5 (not 15) serves the Musée Matisse and Musée National Marc Chagall in the hillside Cimiez neighborhood; bus 82 serves Èze Village; bus 15 serves Villefranche, Beaulieu and St-Jean-Cap-Ferrat
quote: Bus 5 serves the Musée Matisse and Musée National Marc Chagall in the hillside neighbourhood of Cimiez, bus 82 goes to Èze Village, and bus 15 serves Villefranche-sur-Mer, Beaulieu-sur-Mer and St-Jean-Cap-Ferrat

claim: Nice in June: daytime ~24-27°C, nights ~17°C, sea ~23°C, ~12 hours of sunshine, rain rare; June is start of high season but markedly less crowded than July-August peak
quote: Expect 24°C (75°F) during the day and 17°C (63°F) at night... The sea temperature reaches 23°C... June has the most sunshine of the year in Nice with an average of 12 hours of sunshine... Nice in June is lively but not as crowded as the peak summer months of July and August

claim: The 2026 Monaco Grand Prix moves from its traditional late-May slot to June 5-7, 2026 — directly affecting weekend visitors to Nice/Monaco that weekend
quote: The 2026 Monaco Grand Prix takes place in early June, with practice starting on Friday June 5 and the race on Sunday June 7

claim: The 79th Cannes Film Festival ran 12-23 May 2026, with restricted access to the festival zone — a major crowd/price driver in May
quote: The 79th annual Cannes Film Festival took place from 12 to 23 May 2026... Access to the festival zone was restricted to festival-goers from 12 to 23 May, 2026

claim: Jazz à Juan in Juan-les-Pins runs 9-19 July 2026; Nice Jazz Festival runs 23-26 July 2026
quote: The Jazz à Juan Festival runs from 9 to 19 July 2026... The 2026 Nice Jazz Festival takes place 23 – 26 July 2026

claim: Nice Carnival 2026 ran 11 February-1 March with flower battles, illuminated parades and tickets €5-€28 (free in costume)
quote: The carnival kicks off on 11 February with the Grand Charivari and culminates on 28 February... prices from €5 to €28, and the Carnival is free if you attend in costume

claim: Vieux Nice (Old Town) hotels from ~$161/night; Carré d'Or is the central rectangle bounded by Ave Jean Médecin, Bd Victor Hugo, Bd Gambetta and the Promenade; Promenade des Anglais area runs ~17% below the city average of $143
quote: Vieux-Nice hotels have been found for as cheap as $161/night... Le Carré d'Or Area in the city centre covers a rectangular area of Ave Jean Medecin, Bd Victor Hugo, Bd Gambetta and the Promenade... Hotels near Promenade des Anglais are typically 17% less expensive than the average hotel in Nice

claim: Nice is generally safe; main risk is pickpocketing along Promenade des Anglais, in Old Town, at markets and on trams/trains, often by groups using ticket-machine distractions
quote: Pickpockets are very active on the trams/trains and in tourist areas. They operate in groups, usually offering to help you buy a ticket, to distract you and then take what they can

claim: The original Vélo Bleu municipal bike share has been replaced by Pony (blue, e-bikes) and Lime (green) free-floating fleets totalling ~2000 bikes, ~90% electric
quote: The original Velo Bleu system has been replaced by two new bike share fleets with 2000 bikes total, 90% of which are electric. The new blue bikes are operated by Pony... and the Day-Glo green bikes are operated by Lime
